comments.text:
In my experience:- 
1) agar patient male hai aur 50+ to caring treatment nhi hota 

2) Agar cancer stage 1 ya 2 ho to ap private kisi cancer hospital me dikhaye treatment jald hi ho jayegi 

3) Agar apke pass thoda sa bhi paisa nhi hai tbhi aye nhi to stage 1 ya 2 ko stage 4 kar dete hai 

4) agar 18 year below patient hai to free and caring treatment hoga 

5) yaha ladies ko extra help milti hai male ki tulna me
 
4) Agar aap sbhi jagah se treatment kra kr thak gye hai tbhi aye 

5) jb confirm cancer ho to sbhi test report, CD, biopsy slide lekar hi aye 

6) Genral me dikhaye to turant file 'nc' kra le 

7) Agar cancer stage 4 ho to treatment caring nhi hoga 

8) treatment krane ke liye kisi  smjhdarwale person ke sath hi aye 

9) kuch smjh me na aye to apne  opd k kevat se mile

THE DANGERS OF ALLOPATHY
Patient is never considered as a person, but as assembly (assortment) of various organs.
Every drugs are chemicals (in refined/crude form), which are injurious to health, especially if used over a long period of time.
No cure for any diseases, except self-limiting acute diseases.
Since allopathy can't cure any chronic diseases, they increasingly depend  on surgery to prevent recurrence of symptoms. In the process they deprive the body of its original anatomy, necessary for its sustenance.
Allopathic treatment is not based on any philosophy. Only interference with the physiological and biochemical activities of the body using chemicals.
Treatments are mainly aimed at suppressions of the diseases to bring quick relief to the patients. Damage caused to the people by such activities are simply ignored.
Action of drugs are only at tissue level. Hence people with multiple diseases require multiple drugs.
Human body is considered as a machine. Specialists for each organs, the vital energy which synchronise and optimize the activities of different organs and systems is ignored. Hence organ transplantation, fitting artificial parts and replacement therapy have become common practice.
Maintenance of biochemical and physiological values are considered as the aim of treatment. Hence frequent checking of electrolytes and other biochemical values considered as necessary for (supplementation) therapy.
Most of the treatments are interventional, hence complications (even life-threatening) are common.
Since interventional treatments demand a lot of disposable materials and sofisticated equipment, the procedures are exceedingly unaffordable.
Since drugs are mostly strong chemicals, adverse reactions are more or less fatal.
Almost all drugs have serious side effects, which may surpass the disease proper, resulting in organ failure.
They try to overcome the serious flaws in the treatment methods, by including scientific gadgets and innovations to impress upon the patients.
Allopathy is no more a treatment method. But it's part of the health care industry aimed at profiteering, thereby losing any sanctity of service to mankind. Sufferings of people are seen as opportunities for profiteering. Health care professionals are trained to be part of this system of helping each other to mint money.
Allopathy treatment is more or less mechanical and it has become the culture to disregard the patient as an individual. Doctor-patient relationship is almost non-existent.
Flaws in treatment methodology is compensated by gimmicks like calling themselves as ‘modern medicine', ‘scientific medicine', ‘evidence based medicine' etc.. and ridiculing other systems of treatment as pseudoscience to enjoy monopoly in future.
Most of the health-care professionals involved in allopathy are arrogant, contemptuous, greedy, selfish,. and merciless. They have no time to listen to patients or too busy to say kind words to them.
Allopathy treatment is simply unaffordable to the common man, or consciously made so to help health insurance companies.
